```ts
)
const stateArb: fc.Arbitrary<S> = fc.oneof(
	fc.constantFrom<S>({ state: "pending" }, { state: "starting" }, { state: "running" }, { state: "holding" }, { state: "completed" }, { state: "cancelled" }),
	fc.constantFrom(...PAUSED).map((reason): S => ({ state: "paused", reason })),
	fc.constantFrom<FailReason>("source-removed", "tuner-unavailable", "invalid").map((reason): S => ({ state: "failed", reason })),
)

describe("job transition table (§ 10.1)", () => {
	it("starts a sweep with lease, decoder hold and engine; an in-window job only opens the engine", () => {
		const r = transition({ state: "pending" }, { type: "start" })
		expect(r).toEqual({ state: "starting", actions: ["acquire-lease", "hold-decoders", "open-engine"] })
		if ("invalid" in r) return
		expect(actionsForMode("in-window", r.actions)).toEqual(["open-engine"])
		expect(actionsForMode("sweep", r.actions)).toEqual(r.actions)
	})

	it("restores only while the lease is held", () => {
		expect(transition({ state: "running" }, { type: "cancel" })).toEqual({ state: "cancelled", actions: ["stop-probes", "restore", "release-lease", "release-decoders"] })
		expect(transition({ state: "paused", reason: "preempted-operator" }, { type: "cancel" })).toEqual({ state: "cancelled", actions: ["stop-probes"] })
		expect(transition({ state: "holding" }, { type: "stop-condition" })).toEqual({ state: "completed", actions: ["stop-probes", "restore", "release-lease", "release-decoders"] })
		expect(transition({ state: "pending" }, { type: "cancel" })).toEqual({ state: "cancelled", actions: [] })
	})

	it("loses the lease without restoring on an operator write, and hands it over to a higher-priority job", () => {
		expect(transition({ state: "holding" }, { type: "rest-write" })).toEqual({ state: "paused", reason: "preempted-operator", actions: ["stop-probes", "release-lease", "release-decoders"] })
		expect(transition({ state: "running" }, { type: "preempted-job" })).toEqual({ state: "paused", reason: "preempted-job", actions: ["stop-probes", "release-lease"] })
		// a paused lease holder is handed over too, so it never keeps a stale lease
		expect(transition({ state: "paused", reason: "operator" }, { type: "preempted-job" })).toEqual({ state: "paused", reason: "preempted-job", actions: ["release-lease"] })
		expect(transition({ state: "paused", reason: "source-down" }, { type: "preempted-job" })).toEqual({ state: "paused", reason: "preempted-job", actions: ["release-lease"] })
	})

	it("never releases the decoder hold the preemptor owns when a preempted job ends", () => {
		const preempted: S = { state: "paused", reason: "preempted-job" }
		expect(transition(preempted, { type: "cancel" })).toEqual({ state: "cancelled", actions: ["stop-probes"] })
		expect(transition(preempted, { type: "source-removed" })).toEqual({ state: "failed", reason: "source-removed", actions: ["stop-probes"] })
	})

	it("auto-resumes only when the impact did not grow; resume-blocked needs takeover", () => {
		const paused: S = { state: "paused", reason: "preempted-relay" }
		expect(transition(paused, { type: "preemptor-idle", impactGrew: false })).toEqual({ state: "running", actions: ["acquire-lease", "hold-decoders", "resend-hop"] })
		expect(transition(paused, { type: "preemptor-idle", impactGrew: true })).toEqual({ state: "paused", reason: "resume-blocked", actions: ["report-impact", "release-decoders"] })
		expect(transition({ state: "paused", reason: "resume-blocked" }, { type: "resume", takeover: false })).toEqual({ invalid: true })
		expect(transition({ state: "paused", reason: "resume-blocked" }, { type: "resume", takeover: true })).toEqual({ state: "running", actions: ["acquire-lease", "hold-decoders", "resend-hop"] })
	})

	it("resends the hop after a reconnect and restores the persisted lease at boot", () => {
		expect(transition({ state: "paused", reason: "source-down" }, { type: "source-up" })).toEqual({ state: "running", actions: ["resend-hop"] })
		expect(transition({ state: "holding" }, { type: "boot" })).toEqual({ state: "paused", reason: "core-restart", actions: ["restore"] })
		expect(transition({ state: "starting" }, { type: "boot" })).toEqual({ state: "paused", reason: "core-restart", actions: ["restore"] })
		expect(transition({ state: "pending" }, { type: "boot" })).toEqual({ invalid: true })
	})

	// Feature: signal-discovery-scanner, Property 9: Job transitions
	// Validates: spec § 10.1
	it("matches the table exactly for every state × event: listed rows with their actions, INVALID elsewhere", () => {
		expect(ALL_STATES).toHaveLength(16)
		for (const l of ALL_STATES)
			for (const [key, e] of Object.entries(EVENTS)) {
				const want = EXPECTED.get(`${l}|${key}`)
				const r = transition(fromLabel(l), e)
				if (want === undefined) {
					expect({ at: `${l}|${key}`, r }).toEqual({ at: `${l}|${key}`, r: { invalid: true } })
					continue
				}
				const got = "invalid" in r ? r : { to: label(r.reason !== undefined ? { state: r.state, reason: r.reason } : { state: r.state }), actions: r.actions }
				expect({ at: `${l}|${key}`, got }).toEqual({ at: `${l}|${key}`, got: want })
			}
		for (const key of EXPECTED.keys()) expect(ALL_STATES).toContain(key.split("|")[0])
	})

	// Feature: signal-discovery-scanner, Property 9: Job transitions
	// Validates: spec § 10.1
	it("follows the table along any event sequence; terminal states are absorbing; in-window strips lease actions", () => {
		fc.assert(
			fc.property(stateArb, fc.array(eventArb, { maxLength: 40 }), (initial, events) => {
				let s: S = initial
				for (const e of events) {
					const r = transition(s, e)
					const want = EXPECTED.get(`${label(s)}|${eventKey(e)}`)
					if (isTerminal(s.state)) expect(want).toBeUndefined()
					if (want === undefined) {
						expect(r).toEqual({ invalid: true })
						continue
					}
					if ("invalid" in r) throw new Error(`${label(s)}|${eventKey(e)} must be valid`)
					const next: S = r.reason !== undefined ? { state: r.state, reason: r.reason } : { state: r.state }
					expect({ to: label(next), actions: r.actions }).toEqual(want)
					expect(next.state === "paused" || next.state === "failed").toBe(next.reason !== undefined)
					for (const a of actionsForMode("in-window", r.actions))
						expect(["acquire-lease", "release-lease", "restore", "hold-decoders", "release-decoders", "resend-hop"]).not.toContain(a)
					s = next
				}
			}),
			{ numRuns: 100 },
		)
	})
})
```

```ts
// src/core/scanner/job-state.ts
/**
 * Scan job lifecycle (spec § 10.1) as a pure transition function. Actions are those of a sweep;
 * in-window jobs run the same table without the lease rows (`actionsForMode`).
 */
import type { FailReason, JobState, PauseReason, ScanMode } from "./types.js"

export type JobEvent =
	| { type: "start" }
	| { type: "create-rejected" }
	| { type: "engine-ready" }
	| { type: "tuner-error" }
	| { type: "hold" }
	| { type: "hold-done" }
	| { type: "pause" }
	| { type: "rest-write" }
	| { type: "relay-external" }
	| { type: "preempted-job" }
	| { type: "source-down" }
	| { type: "source-up" }
	| { type: "preemptor-idle"; impactGrew: boolean }
	| { type: "resume"; takeover: boolean }
	| { type: "cancel" }
	| { type: "stop-condition" }
	| { type: "source-removed" }
	| { type: "boot" }

export type JobAction =
	| "acquire-lease"
	| "release-lease"
	| "restore"
	| "hold-decoders"
	| "release-decoders"
	| "stop-probes"
	| "open-engine"
	| "resend-hop"
	| "report-impact"

type From = { state: JobState; reason?: PauseReason | FailReason }
type Result = { state: JobState; reason?: PauseReason | FailReason; actions: JobAction[] } | { invalid: true }

const INVALID: Result = { invalid: true }
const TERMINAL: ReadonlySet<JobState> = new Set(["completed", "cancelled", "failed"])
const LEASE_ACTIONS: ReadonlySet<JobAction> = new Set([
	"acquire-lease",
	"release-lease",
	"restore",
	"hold-decoders",
	"release-decoders",
	"resend-hop",
])

export function isTerminal(state: JobState): boolean {
	return TERMINAL.has(state)
}

/** In-window jobs never touch the tuner or the decoder hold (§ 10.1, § 10.3). */
export function actionsForMode(mode: ScanMode, actions: JobAction[]): JobAction[] {
	return mode === "sweep" ? [...actions] : actions.filter(a => !LEASE_ACTIONS.has(a))
}

function to(state: JobState, actions: JobAction[], reason?: PauseReason | FailReason): Result {
	return reason === undefined ? { state, actions } : { state, reason, actions }
}

function holdsLease(s: From): boolean {
	if (s.state === "starting" || s.state === "running" || s.state === "holding") return true
	return s.state === "paused" && (s.reason === "operator" || s.reason === "source-down")
}

/**
 * Ending a job. Only a lease holder restores and releases the lease and its decoder hold. A paused
 * job without the lease (preempted-*, resume-blocked, core-restart) gets stop-probes only: a
 * preempted-job job may still hold its own decoder hold (DecoderManager keys holds by holder,
 * Task 29), which Task 35's terminal teardown drops; the running preemptor's hold is its own key
 * and stays (§ 10.4).
 */
function endActions(s: From): JobAction[] {
	if (s.state === "pending") return []
	return holdsLease(s) ? ["stop-probes", "restore", "release-lease", "release-decoders"] : ["stop-probes"]
}

export function transition(s: From, e: JobEvent): Result {
	if (TERMINAL.has(s.state)) return INVALID
	const active = s.state === "running" || s.state === "holding"
	const pausedFor = (reason: PauseReason): boolean => s.state === "paused" && s.reason === reason
	const preempted = pausedFor("preempted-operator") || pausedFor("preempted-relay") || pausedFor("preempted-job")
	switch (e.type) {
		case "start":
			return s.state === "pending" ? to("starting", ["acquire-lease", "hold-decoders", "open-engine"]) : INVALID
		case "create-rejected":
			return s.state === "pending" ? to("failed", [], "invalid") : INVALID
		case "engine-ready":
			return s.state === "starting" ? to("running", []) : INVALID
		case "tuner-error":
			return s.state === "starting" ? to("failed", ["release-lease", "release-decoders"], "tuner-unavailable") : INVALID
		case "hold":
			return s.state === "running" ? to("holding", []) : INVALID
		case "hold-done":
			return s.state === "holding" ? to("running", []) : INVALID
		case "pause":
			return active ? to("paused", ["stop-probes"], "operator") : INVALID
		case "rest-write":
			return active ? to("paused", ["stop-probes", "release-lease", "release-decoders"], "preempted-operator") : INVALID
		case "relay-external":
			return active ? to("paused", ["stop-probes", "release-lease", "release-decoders"], "preempted-relay") : INVALID
		case "preempted-job":
			if (active) return to("paused", ["stop-probes", "release-lease"], "preempted-job")
			// the arbiter hands the lease over from a paused holder too; probes are already stopped
			return pausedFor("operator") || pausedFor("source-down") ? to("paused", ["release-lease"], "preempted-job") : INVALID
		case "source-down":
			return active ? to("paused", ["stop-probes"], "source-down") : INVALID
		case "source-up":
			return pausedFor("source-down") ? to("running", ["resend-hop"]) : INVALID
		case "preemptor-idle":
			if (!preempted) return INVALID
			return e.impactGrew
				? to("paused", ["report-impact", "release-decoders"], "resume-blocked")
				: to("running", ["acquire-lease", "hold-decoders", "resend-hop"])
		case "resume":
			if (pausedFor("operator")) return to("running", ["resend-hop"])
			if (pausedFor("resume-blocked"))
				return e.takeover ? to("running", ["acquire-lease", "hold-decoders", "resend-hop"]) : INVALID
			if (pausedFor("core-restart")) return to("running", ["acquire-lease", "hold-decoders", "open-engine", "resend-hop"])
			return INVALID
		case "cancel":
			return to("cancelled", endActions(s))
		case "stop-condition":
			return active ? to("completed", endActions(s)) : INVALID
		case "source-removed": {
			if (s.state === "pending") return to("failed", [], "source-removed")
			return to("failed", holdsLease(s) ? ["stop-probes", "release-lease", "release-decoders"] : ["stop-probes"], "source-removed")
		}
		case "boot":
			// a job persisted in starting already held a lease (§ 10.3)
			return s.state === "starting" || active || s.state === "paused" ? to("paused", ["restore"], "core-restart") : INVALID
	}
}
```

### Task 21: WS limiter / coalescer

**Spec:** § 9 (WS row), § 12.2 (rates), § 13 P12. **Depends on:** none. **Batch:** S1-A

**Files:**
- Create: `src/core/scanner/ws-limiter.ts`
- Test: `tests/unit/core/scanner/ws-limiter.test.ts`

Behaviour: one limiter per channel (Task 37 creates the `scanner` one with `maxPerSecond` 10 and `perKeyMinIntervalMs` 1000 for discoveries; progress uses keys `progress:<jobId>` with its own 500 ms limiter or the same limiter, Task 37 decides). `offer(key, msg, priority)` replaces any pending message for the key (latest state wins, the key keeps its queue position and the higher priority). An emission needs a free slot in the sliding 1 s window (`< maxPerSecond` emissions in `(now − 1000, now]`) and `now − lastEmit(key) ≥ perKeyMinIntervalMs`; among eligible keys `state` beats `progress` beats `activity`, then the oldest offer. When something is pending but nothing is eligible, one timer is armed for the earliest instant something becomes eligible, so the latest state of every key is always delivered. Pending `activity` messages are bounded at 256 (the oldest activity is dropped: "newest wins"); `state`/`progress` keys are never dropped. `flush()` emits everything pending immediately, ignoring the limits (shutdown only); `setMaxPerSecond(n)` applies a runtime `ws.maxMessagesPerSecond` change (Tasks 37/37a call it on a settings PATCH; lowering holds new emissions until the window drains, raising releases pending keys at once); `destroy()` cancels the timer and drops everything.

```ts
// tests/unit/core/scanner/ws-limiter.test.ts
import fc from "fast-check"
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"
import { WsLimiter } from "../../../../src/core/scanner/ws-limiter.js"

interface Msg {
	key: string
	version: number
}

class FakeClock {
	t = 0
	private seq = 0
	private tasks: { at: number; seq: number; fn: () => void; cancelled: boolean }[] = []
	now = (): number => this.t
	schedule = (fn: () => void, ms: number): { cancel(): void } => {
		const task = { at: this.t + ms, seq: this.seq++, fn, cancelled: false }
		this.tasks.push(task)
		return { cancel: () => { task.cancelled = true } }
	}
	advanceTo(target: number): void {
		for (;;) {
			const due = this.tasks.filter(x => !x.cancelled && x.at <= target).sort((a, b) => a.at - b.at || a.seq - b.seq)[0]
			if (due === undefined) break
			this.tasks = this.tasks.filter(x => x !== due)
			this.t = Math.max(this.t, due.at)
			due.fn()
		}
		this.t = Math.max(this.t, target)
	}
}

function setup(maxPerSecond: number, perKeyMinIntervalMs: number) {
	const clock = new FakeClock()
	const emitted: { at: number; msg: Msg }[] = []
	const limiter = new WsLimiter<Msg>({ maxPerSecond, perKeyMinIntervalMs, now: clock.now, emit: msg => emitted.push({ at: clock.t, msg }), schedule: clock.schedule })
	return { clock, emitted, limiter }
}

describe("WsLimiter", () => {
	it("coalesces bursts per key to the latest state, at most once per interval", () => {
		const { clock, emitted, limiter } = setup(10, 1_000)
		for (let v = 1; v <= 5; v++) {
			clock.advanceTo(v * 100)
			limiter.offer("d1", { key: "d1", version: v }, "state")
		}
		clock.advanceTo(5_000)
		expect(emitted).toEqual([
			{ at: 100, msg: { key: "d1", version: 1 } },
			{ at: 1_100, msg: { key: "d1", version: 5 } },
		])
	})

	it("caps the total rate and prefers state over activity when slots are scarce", () => {
		const { clock, emitted, limiter } = setup(2, 0)
		limiter.offer("a1", { key: "a1", version: 1 }, "activity")
		limiter.offer("a2", { key: "a2", version: 1 }, "activity")
		limiter.offer("a3", { key: "a3", version: 1 }, "activity")
		limiter.offer("s1", { key: "s1", version: 1 }, "state")
		expect(emitted.map(e => e.msg.key)).toEqual(["a1", "a2"])
		clock.advanceTo(1_000)
		expect(emitted.map(e => e.msg.key)).toEqual(["a1", "a2", "s1", "a3"])
		expect(emitted.map(e => e.at)).toEqual([0, 0, 1_000, 1_000])
	})

	it("flushes pending messages and goes silent after destroy", () => {
		const { clock, emitted, limiter } = setup(1, 1_000)
		limiter.offer("d1", { key: "d1", version: 1 }, "state")
		limiter.offer("d2", { key: "d2", version: 1 }, "state")
		limiter.flush()
		expect(emitted.map(e => e.msg.key)).toEqual(["d1", "d2"])
		limiter.offer("d3", { key: "d3", version: 1 }, "state")
		limiter.offer("d4", { key: "d4", version: 1 }, "state")
		limiter.destroy()
		limiter.offer("d5", { key: "d5", version: 1 }, "state")
		clock.advanceTo(10_000)
		expect(emitted.map(e => e.msg.key)).toEqual(["d1", "d2"])
	})

	it("applies a runtime maxPerSecond change", () => {
		const { clock, emitted, limiter } = setup(2, 0)
		for (const key of ["s1", "s2", "s3", "s4"]) limiter.offer(key, { key, version: 1 }, "state")
		expect(emitted.map(e => e.msg.key)).toEqual(["s1", "s2"])
		limiter.setMaxPerSecond(4)
		expect(emitted.map(e => e.msg.key)).toEqual(["s1", "s2", "s3", "s4"])
		expect(emitted.map(e => e.at)).toEqual([0, 0, 0, 0])
		limiter.setMaxPerSecond(1)
		limiter.offer("s5", { key: "s5", version: 1 }, "state")
		clock.advanceTo(999)
		expect(emitted).toHaveLength(4)
		clock.advanceTo(1_000)
		expect(emitted.map(e => e.msg.key)).toEqual(["s1", "s2", "s3", "s4", "s5"])
		expect(emitted.at(-1)?.at).toBe(1_000)
	})

	// Feature: signal-discovery-scanner, Property 12: WS rate limits

	it("respects the window and per-key limits and eventually delivers every key's latest state", () => {
		const offerArb = fc.record({

		})
		fc.assert(

				const { clock, emitted, limiter } = setup(max, interval)

					limiter.offer(key, { key, version: i }, o.priority)
				})

				const lastByKey = new Map<string, { at: number; version: number }>()
				for (const e of emitted) {
					const prev = lastByKey.get(e.msg.key)
					if (prev !== undefined) {
						expect(e.at - prev.at).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(interval)
						expect(e.msg.version).toBeGreaterThan(prev.version)
					}
					lastByKey.set(e.msg.key, { at: e.at, version: e.msg.version })
				}
				for (const [key, version] of latest) expect(lastByKey.get(key)?.version).toBe(version)
			}),
			{ numRuns: 100 },
		)
	})
})
```

```ts
// src/core/scanner/ws-limiter.ts
/**
 * Rate limiter and coalescer for scanner WebSocket messages (spec § 9, § 12.2): at most
 * `maxPerSecond` emissions in any 1 s window, at most one per key per `perKeyMinIntervalMs`, latest
 * state per key wins, and the latest state of every key is always delivered eventually.
 */
type Priority = "state" | "progress" | "activity"

const WINDOW_MS = 1_000
const MAX_PENDING_ACTIVITY = 256
const LAST_EMIT_PRUNE_SIZE = 1_024
const RANK: Record<Priority, number> = { state: 0, progress: 1, activity: 2 }

interface Pending<T> {
	msg: T
	priority: Priority
	seq: number
}

export class WsLimiter<T> {
	private maxPerSecond: number
	private readonly perKeyMinIntervalMs: number
	private readonly now: () => number
	private readonly emitFn: (msg: T) => void
	private readonly scheduleFn: (fn: () => void, ms: number) => { cancel(): void }
	private readonly pending = new Map<string, Pending<T>>()
	private readonly lastEmit = new Map<string, number>()
	private readonly window: number[] = []
	private timer: { cancel(): void } | null = null
	private timerAt = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
	private seq = 0
	private destroyed = false

	constructor(opts: {
		maxPerSecond: number
		perKeyMinIntervalMs: number
		now: () => number
		emit: (msg: T) => void
		schedule: (fn: () => void, ms: number) => { cancel(): void }
	}) {
		this.maxPerSecond = Math.max(1, Math.floor(opts.maxPerSecond))
		this.perKeyMinIntervalMs = Math.max(0, opts.perKeyMinIntervalMs)
		this.now = opts.now
		this.emitFn = opts.emit
		this.scheduleFn = opts.schedule
	}

	offer(key: string, msg: T, priority: Priority): void {
		if (this.destroyed) return
		const existing = this.pending.get(key)
		if (existing !== undefined) {
			existing.msg = msg
			if (RANK[priority] < RANK[existing.priority]) existing.priority = priority
		} else {
			this.pending.set(key, { msg, priority, seq: this.seq++ })
			if (priority === "activity") this.boundActivity()
		}
		this.pump()
	}

	/** Emits everything pending now, ignoring the limits (shutdown only). */
	flush(): void {
		if (this.destroyed) return
		this.cancelTimer()
		const now = this.now()
		const entries = [...this.pending].sort(([, a], [, b]) => RANK[a.priority] - RANK[b.priority] || a.seq - b.seq)
		this.pending.clear()
		for (const [key, entry] of entries) this.emit(key, entry.msg, now)
	}

	/** Runtime update of `ws.maxMessagesPerSecond` (settings PATCH, Task 37). Lowering it holds back new emissions until the window drains; raising it releases pending keys now. */
	setMaxPerSecond(maxPerSecond: number): void {
		this.maxPerSecond = Math.max(1, Math.floor(maxPerSecond))
		this.pump()
	}

	destroy(): void {
		this.destroyed = true
		this.cancelTimer()
		this.pending.clear()
	}

	private pump(): void {
		if (this.destroyed) return
		const now = this.now()
		this.prune(now)
		while (this.window.length < this.maxPerSecond) {
			const next = this.nextEligible(now)
			if (next === null) break
			this.pending.delete(next[0])
			this.emit(next[0], next[1].msg, now)
		}
		this.arm(now)
	}

	private emit(key: string, msg: T, now: number): void {
		this.window.push(now)
		this.lastEmit.set(key, now)
		this.emitFn(msg)
	}

	private nextEligible(now: number): [string, Pending<T>] | null {
		let best: [string, Pending<T>] | null = null
		for (const [key, entry] of this.pending) {
			const last = this.lastEmit.get(key)
			if (last !== undefined && now - last < this.perKeyMinIntervalMs) continue
			if (best === null || RANK[entry.priority] < RANK[best[1].priority] || (RANK[entry.priority] === RANK[best[1].priority] && entry.seq < best[1].seq))
				best = [key, entry]
		}
		return best
	}

	private arm(now: number): void {
		if (this.pending.size === 0) {
			this.cancelTimer()
			return
		}
		// After a runtime lowering the window can hold more than `maxPerSecond` entries: the next slot frees
		// when the entry `maxPerSecond` from the newest leaves the window.
		const windowFree = this.window.length >= this.maxPerSecond ? (this.window[this.window.length - this.maxPerSecond] ?? now) + WINDOW_MS : now
		let at = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
		for (const key of this.pending.keys()) {
			const last = this.lastEmit.get(key)
			const keyFree = last === undefined ? now : last + this.perKeyMinIntervalMs
			at = Math.min(at, Math.max(keyFree, windowFree))
		}
		if (this.timer !== null && this.timerAt === at) return
		this.cancelTimer()
		this.timerAt = at
		this.timer = this.scheduleFn(() => {
			this.timer = null
			this.timerAt = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
			this.pump()
		}, Math.max(0, at - now))
	}

	private prune(now: number): void {
		while (this.window.length > 0 && now - (this.window[0] ?? now) >= WINDOW_MS) this.window.shift()
		if (this.lastEmit.size > LAST_EMIT_PRUNE_SIZE)
			for (const [key, at] of this.lastEmit) if (now - at >= this.perKeyMinIntervalMs && !this.pending.has(key)) this.lastEmit.delete(key)
	}

	private boundActivity(): void {
		let count = 0
		let oldest: [string, number] | null = null
		for (const [key, entry] of this.pending) {
			if (entry.priority !== "activity") continue
			count++
			if (oldest === null || entry.seq < oldest[1]) oldest = [key, entry.seq]
		}
		if (count > MAX_PENDING_ACTIVITY && oldest !== null) this.pending.delete(oldest[0])
	}

	private cancelTimer(): void {
		this.timer?.cancel()
		this.timer = null
		this.timerAt = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
	}
}
```

**Spec:** § 9 (host CPU guard: `1 − idle` from `os.cpus()` deltas over 5 s, or cgroup usage ÷ quota cores inside a container; no metric → budget-only admission), § 12.1 (status shows metric and threshold). Plan-time fact: `packages/api-types/src/resources.ts` `cpuUsagePercent` is cgroup-only and not normalised, so it is not reused. **Depends on:** none. **Batch:** S1-A

**Files:**

- Test: `tests/unit/core/scanner/cpu-meter.test.ts`

Behaviour: `mode` is the requested `source`, or `cgroup` when `cpu.max` holds a quota (`"<quota> <period>"`, a container limit) and `os` otherwise. `os`: percent = 100 × Δbusy / Δtotal summed over all CPUs (busy = user + nice + sys + irq), already normalised to the host. `cgroup`: percent = 100 × Δ`usage_usec` / (Δwall µs × cores), cores = quota / period, or the CPU count when `cpu.max` is `max`. The first sample only primes; unreadable or empty inputs reset the value to `null` (admission is then budget-only); results clamp to 0–100. `start()` samples immediately and every `sampleMs` (5000 in Task 35) on an unref'd interval.

```ts
// src/core/scanner/cpu-meter.ts
/**
 * Normalised host CPU for the probe admission guard (spec § 9): `1 − idle` over `os.cpus()` deltas,
 * or cgroup v2 `usage_usec` over the quota's cores inside a CPU-limited container. `null` when no
 * metric is available (admission is then budget-only).
 */
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { cpus } from "node:os"
import { performance } from "node:perf_hooks"

export interface CpuReaders {
	cpus?: () => readonly { times: { user: number; nice: number; sys: number; idle: number; irq: number } }[]
	readCgroup?: (file: "cpu.stat" | "cpu.max") => string | null
	now?: () => number
}

const CGROUP_ROOT = "/sys/fs/cgroup"
const USAGE_USEC = /^usage_usec\s+(\d+)\s*$/m

function readCgroupFile(file: "cpu.stat" | "cpu.max"): string | null {
	try {
		return readFileSync(`${CGROUP_ROOT}/${file}`, "utf8")
	} catch {
		return null
	}
}

const clampPercent = (v: number): number => Math.min(100, Math.max(0, v))

export class CpuMeter {
	private readonly sampleMs: number
	private readonly requested: "os" | "cgroup" | undefined
	private readonly readCpus: NonNullable<CpuReaders["cpus"]>
	private readonly readCgroup: NonNullable<CpuReaders["readCgroup"]>
	private readonly clock: NonNullable<CpuReaders["now"]>
	private timer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null
	private prevOs: { busy: number; total: number } | null = null
	private prevCgroup: { usageUsec: number; at: number } | null = null
	private value: number | null = null

	constructor(opts: { sampleMs: number; source?: "os" | "cgroup"; readers?: CpuReaders }) {
		this.sampleMs = opts.sampleMs
		this.requested = opts.source
		this.readCpus = opts.readers?.cpus ?? cpus
		this.readCgroup = opts.readers?.readCgroup ?? readCgroupFile
		this.clock = opts.readers?.now ?? (() => performance.now())
	}

	get mode(): "os" | "cgroup" {
		return this.requested ?? (this.quotaCores() !== null ? "cgroup" : "os")
	}

	get normalisedPercent(): number | null {
		return this.value
	}

	start(): void {
		if (this.timer !== null) return
		this.sample()
		this.timer = setInterval(() => this.sample(), this.sampleMs)
		this.timer.unref()
	}

	stop(): void {
		if (this.timer !== null) clearInterval(this.timer)
		this.timer = null
	}

	sample(): void {
		if (this.mode === "cgroup") this.sampleCgroup()
		else this.sampleOs()
	}

	private sampleOs(): void {
		const list = this.readCpus()
		if (list.length === 0) {
			this.value = null
			this.prevOs = null
			return
		}
		let busy = 0
		let total = 0
		for (const c of list) {
			const t = c.times
			const all = t.user + t.nice + t.sys + t.idle + t.irq
			total += all
			busy += all - t.idle
		}
		const prev = this.prevOs
		this.prevOs = { busy, total }
		if (prev === null) return
		const dTotal = total - prev.total
		if (dTotal <= 0) return
		this.value = clampPercent((100 * (busy - prev.busy)) / dTotal)
	}

	private sampleCgroup(): void {
		const stat = this.readCgroup("cpu.stat")
		const match = stat === null ? null : USAGE_USEC.exec(stat)
		const cores = this.quotaCores() ?? this.readCpus().length
		if (match === null || cores <= 0) {
			this.value = null
			this.prevCgroup = null
			return
		}
		const usageUsec = Number(match[1])
		const at = this.clock()
		const prev = this.prevCgroup
		this.prevCgroup = { usageUsec, at }
		if (prev === null) return
		const wallMs = at - prev.at
		if (wallMs <= 0) return
		this.value = clampPercent((100 * (usageUsec - prev.usageUsec)) / (wallMs * 1000 * cores))
	}

	/** Cores granted by cgroup v2 `cpu.max` ("<quota> <period>"), or null without a quota. */
	private quotaCores(): number | null {
		const max = this.readCgroup("cpu.max")
		if (max === null) return null
		const [quota, period] = max.trim().split(/\s+/)
		if (quota === undefined || quota === "max") return null
		const q = Number(quota)
		const p = Number(period ?? "100000")
		return Number.isFinite(q) && Number.isFinite(p) && q > 0 && p > 0 ? q / p : null
	}
}
```

```ts
describe("SCANNER_SETTINGS_BOUNDS agree with the config schema", () => {

		([, b]) => b.type === "number" || b.type === "integer",
	)
	it.each(numeric)("%s accepts its min and max and rejects just outside", (key, bounds) => {
		const patch = (value: number) => {
			const parts = key.split(".")
			const leaf = parts.pop()!
			const root: Record<string, unknown> = {}
			let node = root
			for (const part of parts) {
				const child: Record<string, unknown> = {}
				node[part] = child
				node = child
			}
			node[leaf] = value
			return root
		}
		const step = bounds.type === "integer" ? 1 : 0.001
		expect(ScannerSettingsPatchSchema.safeParse(patch(bounds.min!)).success).toBe(true)
		expect(ScannerSettingsPatchSchema.safeParse(patch(bounds.max!)).success).toBe(true)
		expect(ScannerSettingsPatchSchema.safeParse(patch(bounds.min! - step)).success).toBe(false)
		expect(ScannerSettingsPatchSchema.safeParse(patch(bounds.max! + step)).success).toBe(false)
		expect(ScannerConfigSchema.safeParse(patch(bounds.min!)).success).toBe(true)
		expect(ScannerConfigSchema.safeParse(patch(bounds.max!)).success).toBe(true)
	})
})
```

```ts
const POWER_OF_TWO_FFT = z
	.number()
	.int()
	.min(512)
	.max(16384)
	.refine(n => (n & (n - 1)) === 0, "fftSize must be a power of two")

/**
 * Signal discovery scanner (spec § 12.3). Every key has a default, so an
 * absent section enables the scanner with passive in-window discovery.
 */
export const ScannerConfigSchema = z
	.object({
		enabled: z.boolean().default(true),
		passive: z
			.object({
				enabled: z.boolean().default(true),
				/** Pre-channelizer offset probes for passive jobs (each costs a full-rate chain). */
				offsetProbes: z.boolean().default(false),
			})
			.default({}),
		cpuBudgetCores: z.number().finite().min(0.1).max(64).default(1),
		cpuGuardPercent: z.number().finite().min(1).max(100).default(90),
		maxProbes: z
			.object({
				offset: z.number().int().min(0).max(16).default(1),
				channel: z.number().int().min(0).max(64).default(4),
			})
			.default({}),
		ringSeconds: z.number().finite().min(0.5).max(30).default(3),
		detection: z
			.object({
				fftSize: z.union([z.literal("auto"), POWER_OF_TWO_FFT]).default("auto"),
				integrationMs: z.number().finite().min(5).max(1000).default(50),
				sensitivity: z.enum(["low", "normal", "high"]).default("normal"),
				faTargetPerMhzMin: z.number().finite().min(0.01).max(1000).default(1),
				dcGuardHz: z.number().finite().min(0).max(100_000).default(1500),
				ppmMargin: z.number().finite().min(0).max(100).default(2),
				clipFraction: z.number().finite().min(1e-6).max(1).default(0.001),
				hysteresisDb: z.number().finite().min(0).max(20).default(3),
				minSurfaceBlocks: z.number().int().min(1).max(20).default(2),
				/** Short-burst path (§ 4.10); null disables it. */
				shortIntegrationMs: z.number().positive().nullable().default(5),
				/** FFT frame overlap (§ 4.2): 0 or 0.5. */
				overlap: z.union([z.literal(0), z.literal(0.5)]).default(0),
			})
			.default({}),
		sweep: z
			.object({
				markers: z.boolean().default(true),
				markerTimeoutMs: z.number().int().min(100).max(10_000).default(2000),
```

```ts
// src/core/scanner/settings.ts
/**
 * Runtime scanner settings (spec § 12.1 GET/PATCH /api/scanner/settings,
 * plan D4): config merged with persisted runtime overrides, with the
 * provenance of every leaf and the bounds the UI may offer.
 */
import {
	RuntimeSettingsOverridesSchema,
	type RuntimeSettingsOverrides,
} from "./store/persistence.js"
import {
	ScannerConfigSchema,
	sourceScannerConfig,
	type SourceConfig,
} from "../../config.js"
import type { ScannerSettings } from "./types.js"

export type ScannerSettingProvenance = "config" | "runtime" | "default"

export interface ScannerSettingBounds {
	type: "number" | "integer" | "boolean" | "string"
	min?: number
	max?: number
	enum?: string[]
}

interface NumericBounds {
	type: "number" | "integer"
	min: number
	max: number
}

/** Runtime-safe numeric keys (spec § 12.1); the config schema uses the same limits. */
const NUMERIC_BOUNDS = {
	cpuBudgetCores: { type: "number", min: 0.1, max: 64 },
	"maxProbes.offset": { type: "integer", min: 0, max: 16 },
	"maxProbes.channel": { type: "integer", min: 0, max: 64 },
	"detection.integrationMs": { type: "number", min: 5, max: 1000 },
	"detection.faTargetPerMhzMin": { type: "number", min: 0.01, max: 1000 },
	"detection.hysteresisDb": { type: "number", min: 0, max: 20 },
	"detection.minSurfaceBlocks": { type: "integer", min: 1, max: 20 },
	"storage.maxRecordingsMb": { type: "integer", min: 1, max: 1_000_000 },
	"storage.maxEvidenceMb": { type: "integer", min: 1, max: 100_000 },
	"storage.maxJournalMb": { type: "integer", min: 1, max: 10_000 },
	"storage.maxAgeDays": { type: "integer", min: 1, max: 3650 },
	"storage.discoveryMaxAgeDays": { type: "integer", min: 1, max: 3650 },
	"storage.minFreeDiskMb": { type: "integer", min: 0, max: 1_000_000 },
	"storage.maxDiscoveries": { type: "integer", min: 1, max: 1_000_000 },
	"storage.maxCapturesMb": { type: "integer", min: 1, max: 100_000 },
	"ws.maxMessagesPerSecond": { type: "integer", min: 1, max: 100 },
	"ws.spectrumHz": { type: "number", min: 0.5, max: 25 },
	"ws.spectrumBins": { type: "integer", min: 128, max: 2048 },
} as const satisfies Record<string, NumericBounds>

export const SCANNER_SETTINGS_BOUNDS: Readonly<
	Record<string, ScannerSettingBounds>
> = {
	...NUMERIC_BOUNDS,
	"detection.sensitivity": { type: "string", enum: ["low", "normal", "high"] },
	"passive.<sourceId>": { type: "boolean" },
}

/**
 * PATCH /api/scanner/settings body. It is Task 16's RuntimeSettingsOverridesSchema (settings.json)
 * itself, not a copy: whatever settings.json loads, a later PATCH re-parses without error, and
 * every accepted PATCH reloads. NUMERIC_BOUNDS above mirrors its limits for the GET view; the
 * "SCANNER_SETTINGS_BOUNDS agree" test fails if they drift.
 */
export const ScannerSettingsPatchSchema = RuntimeSettingsOverridesSchema

export interface EffectiveScannerSettings {
	settings: ScannerSettings
	passiveBySource: Record<string, boolean>
	/** Dotted leaf path ("detection.integrationMs", "passive.<sourceId>") → origin. */
	provenance: Record<string, ScannerSettingProvenance>
}

type Tree = Record<string, unknown>

function isTree(value: unknown): value is Tree {
	return typeof value === "object" && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)
}

/** Leaf [path, value] pairs of a plain object tree (arrays and null are leaves). */
function leaves(value: unknown, prefix = ""): [string, unknown][] {
	if (!isTree(value)) return [[prefix, value]]
	return Object.entries(value).flatMap(([key, child]) =>
		leaves(child, prefix ? `${prefix}.${key}` : key),
	)
}

function readPath(tree: Tree, path: string): unknown {
	let node: unknown = tree
	for (const part of path.split(".")) {
		if (!isTree(node)) return undefined
		node = node[part]
	}
	return node
}

function writePath(tree: Tree, path: string, value: unknown): void {
	const parts = path.split(".")
	const leaf = parts.pop()
	if (leaf === undefined) return
	let node = tree
	for (const part of parts) {
		const child = node[part]
		if (isTree(child)) {
			node = child
		} else {
			const created: Tree = {}
			node[part] = created
			node = created
		}
	}
	node[leaf] = value
}

const DEFAULTS: ScannerSettings = ScannerConfigSchema.parse({})

/**
 * Config + runtime overrides. A configured value equal to its default is
 * reported as "default": it is indistinguishable after parsing and behaves
 * identically.
 */
export function mergeScannerSettings(input: {
	config: ScannerSettings
	sources: readonly Pick<SourceConfig, "id" | "scanner">[]
	overrides: RuntimeSettingsOverrides
}): EffectiveScannerSettings {
	const settings = structuredClone(input.config)
	const tree = settings as unknown as Tree
	const provenance: Record<string, ScannerSettingProvenance> = {}
	for (const [path, value] of leaves(input.config)) {
		provenance[path] =
			value === readPath(DEFAULTS as unknown as Tree, path) ? "default" : "config"
	}
	const { passive, ...rest } = input.overrides
	for (const [path, value] of leaves(rest)) {
		if (value === undefined || path === "") continue
		writePath(tree, path, value)
		provenance[path] = "runtime"
	}
	const passiveBySource: Record<string, boolean> = {}
	for (const source of input.sources) {
		const override = passive?.[source.id]
		const configured = sourceScannerConfig(source).passive
		passiveBySource[source.id] =
			settings.passive.enabled && (override ?? configured)
		provenance[`passive.${source.id}`] =
			override !== undefined
				? "runtime"
				: source.scanner !== undefined
					? "config"
					: "default"
	}
	return { settings, passiveBySource, provenance }
}

/** Applies a validated PATCH to the persisted overrides; throws ZodError when invalid. */
export function applySettingsPatch(
	current: RuntimeSettingsOverrides,
	patch: RuntimeSettingsOverrides,
): RuntimeSettingsOverrides {
	const valid = ScannerSettingsPatchSchema.parse(patch)
	const { passive, ...rest } = valid
	const next = structuredClone(current) as Tree
	for (const [path, value] of leaves(rest)) {
		if (value !== undefined && path !== "") writePath(next, path, value)
	}
	if (passive !== undefined) {
		next["passive"] = { ...(current.passive ?? {}), ...passive }
	}
	return ScannerSettingsPatchSchema.parse(next)
}
```

`RuntimeSettingsOverridesSchema` and its `z.infer` type `RuntimeSettingsOverrides` are defined once, in Task 16's `store/persistence.ts`; this file re-exports the schema as `ScannerSettingsPatchSchema` (so `PATCH` and `settings.json` can never disagree) and keeps `NUMERIC_BOUNDS` only to publish the bounds in `GET /api/scanner/settings`. The bounds test in Step 2 checks every `NUMERIC_BOUNDS` entry against the shared schema and the config schema. `cpuGuardPercent` is config-only (not a § 12.1 runtime row), so neither the schema nor `NUMERIC_BOUNDS` lists it.

Adding `"tuner-scanning"` to the shared union here makes it a public code with no change to the channelizer's mapping; the status DTO shows `suspended: true, suspension: { reasonCode: "tuner-scanning", since }`. `decoder-rate-schemas.ts` is the only Fastify enum that carries the suspension codes (`decoder-status-schemas.ts` imports it).

```ts
// tests/unit/api/scanner-dto-contract.test.ts
/**
 * Scanner DTO contract (spec § 12.4): new DecoderStatus fields and the
 * tuner-scanning reason survive the Fastify response schema, the
 * decoder:status serializer emits the same body, and the api-types scanner
 * DTOs stay identical to the core types they mirror.
 */
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest"
import Fastify, { type FastifyInstance } from "fastify"
import type * as Api from "@wavekit/api-types"
import { decoderRoutes, type DecoderRoutesOptions } from "../../../src/api/routes/decoders.js"
import { toApiDecoderInfo } from "../../../src/api/serializers/decoder-status.js"
import type * as Core from "../../../src/core/scanner/types.js"
import type { DecoderCaps, DecoderStatus } from "../../../src/decoders/types.js"

type Same<A, B> = [A] extends [B] ? ([B] extends [A] ? true : false) : false
// Compile-time drift guard (checked by `pnpm run typecheck`): the DTOs are copies.
const sameShapes: [
	Same<Api.Discovery, Core.Discovery>,
	Same<Api.Observation, Core.Observation>,
	Same<Api.ScanJobSpec, Core.ScanJobSpec>,
	Same<Api.NormalisedJobSpec, Core.NormalisedJobSpec>,
	Same<Api.HopPlan, Core.HopPlan>,
	Same<Api.PlanPreview, Core.PlanPreview>,
	Same<Api.Impact, Core.Impact>,
	Same<Api.PlanIssue, Core.PlanIssue>,
	Same<Api.ScannerSettingsValues, Core.ScannerSettings>,
	Same<Api.ScannerProtocol, Core.ScannerProtocol>,
] = [true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true]

const caps: DecoderCaps = { input: "iq", output: "text", integrationPattern: "pure_consumer" }
/** One registry for the route and the WS serializer, as in production (routes/decoders.ts, server.ts). */
const decoderRegistry = {
	getCaps: () => caps,
	getRegisteredTypes: () => ["dsd-fme"],
} as unknown as DecoderRoutesOptions["decoderRegistry"]

function probeStatus(): DecoderStatus {
	return {
		id: "scan-abc1234-dmr-1",
		type: "dsd-fme",
		running: true,
		health: "running",
		uptime: 3,
		stats: { bytesIn: 10, eventsOut: 1, errors: 0 },
		restartCount: 0,
		desiredRunning: true,
		suspended: false,
		sourceId: "rtl",
		owner: "scanner",
		scannerJobId: "j_01JABCDEF",
		ephemeral: true,
	}
}

function heldStatus(): DecoderStatus {
	return {
		id: "dmr",
		type: "dsd-fme",
		running: false,
		health: "running",
		uptime: 0,
		stats: { bytesIn: 0, eventsOut: 0, errors: 0 },
		restartCount: 0,
		desiredRunning: true,
		suspended: true,
		suspension: { reasonCode: "tuner-scanning", since: new Date("2026-10-09T12:00:00.000Z") },
		sourceId: "rtl",
		owner: "config",
	}
}

describe("scanner DecoderStatus fields over REST and WS", () => {
	let app: FastifyInstance
	let statuses: DecoderStatus[]

	beforeEach(async () => {
		statuses = [probeStatus(), heldStatus()]
		app = Fastify()
		await app.register(decoderRoutes, {
			decoderManager: {
				getAllStatus: () => statuses,
				getStatus: (id: string) => statuses.find(s => s.id === id),
				getDecoder: (id: string) => {
					const s = statuses.find(x => x.id === id)
					return s ? { caps, getStatus: () => s } : undefined
				},
			} as unknown as DecoderRoutesOptions["decoderManager"],
			decoderRegistry,
		})
	})
	afterEach(async () => {
		await app.close()
	})

	it("keeps owner, scannerJobId and ephemeral on a probe", async () => {
		const body = (await app.inject("/api/decoders")).json() as Record<string, unknown>[]
		expect(body[0]).toMatchObject({ owner: "scanner", scannerJobId: "j_01JABCDEF", ephemeral: true })
		expect(body[1]?.["owner"]).toBe("config")
		expect(body[1]).not.toHaveProperty("ephemeral")
		expect(body[1]).not.toHaveProperty("scannerJobId")
	})

	it("reports a held configured decoder as suspended for tuner-scanning", async () => {
		const body = (await app.inject("/api/decoders/dmr")).json() as Record<string, unknown>
		expect(body).toMatchObject({
			suspended: true,
			suspension: { reasonCode: "tuner-scanning", since: "2026-10-09T12:00:00.000Z" },
		})
	})

	it("the decoder:status payload equals the REST body", async () => {
		for (const status of statuses) {
			const rest = (await app.inject(`/api/decoders/${status.id}`)).json() as unknown
			const ws = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(toApiDecoderInfo(status, decoderRegistry))) as unknown
			expect(ws).toEqual(rest)
		}
	})

	it("the DTO copies match the core types", () => {
		expect(sameShapes.every(Boolean)).toBe(true)
	})
})
```

Always pass the same registry the route uses: `GET /api/decoders/:id` calls `toApiDecoderInfo(status, decoderRegistry)` (`src/api/routes/decoders.ts`) and the production `decoder:status` broadcast calls `toApiDecoderInfo(status, this.decoderRegistry)` (`src/api/server.ts`). Without it the serializer omits `caps` and the WS body cannot equal the REST body.

### Task 26: SourceManager — align S16_IQ and FLOAT32LE IQ chunks

**Spec:** § 4.1 (alignment), C4. **Depends on:** 23. **Batch:** S1-B

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/core/source-manager.ts` (new exported `iqFrameBytes`, `alignIqChunk` above `class SourceManager`; `forwardData` alignment block, today :394-405)
- Test: `tests/unit/core/iq-frame-alignment.test.ts` (append a `describe`)

Today only `U8_IQ` chunks are cut to whole I/Q pairs; fanout sheds whole chunks, so an S16 or F32 chunk that ends mid-sample shifts every later sample of every consumer by one component (I/Q swap, garbage spectrum). Frame sizes are 2 (U8 pair), 4 (S16 pair), 8 (F32 pair), the same values as Task 4's `bytesPerSample(format)`. The helper is local to the source manager so core does not import scanner modules.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

Append to `tests/unit/core/iq-frame-alignment.test.ts` (it already has `import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest"`, which covers every name below; add `import * as fc from "fast-check"` and extend the source-manager import to `import { SourceManager, alignIqChunk, iqFrameBytes } from "../../../src/core/source-manager.js"`):

```ts
describe("IQ frame alignment for every IQ format", () => {
	it("frame sizes: U8 pair 2, S16 pair 4, F32 pair 8; audio and auto are not aligned", () => {
		expect(iqFrameBytes({ kind: "iq", format: "U8_IQ" })).toBe(2)
		expect(iqFrameBytes({ kind: "iq", format: "S16_IQ" })).toBe(4)
		expect(iqFrameBytes({ kind: "iq", format: "FLOAT32LE" })).toBe(8)
		expect(iqFrameBytes({ kind: "audio_pcm", format: "FLOAT32LE" })).toBeNull()
		expect(iqFrameBytes({ kind: "audio_pcm", format: "S16LE" })).toBeNull()
		expect(iqFrameBytes({ kind: "iq", format: "auto" })).toBeNull()
	})

	it("any split of a stream yields whole frames, in order, losing only the unfinished tail", () => {
		fc.assert(
			fc.property(
				fc.constantFrom(2, 4, 8),
				fc.uint8Array({ minLength: 0, maxLength: 400 }),
				fc.array(fc.integer({ min: 1, max: 37 }), { minLength: 1, maxLength: 40 }),
				(frame, bytes, cuts) => {
					const data = Buffer.from(bytes)
					let remainder: Buffer = Buffer.alloc(0)
					const out: Buffer[] = []
					let offset = 0
					let i = 0
					while (offset < data.length) {
						const length = cuts[i++ % cuts.length]!
						const result = alignIqChunk(remainder, data.subarray(offset, offset + length), frame)
						offset += length
						expect(result.aligned.length % frame).toBe(0)
						expect(result.remainder.length).toBeLessThan(frame)
						out.push(result.aligned)
						remainder = result.remainder
					}
					const whole = data.length - (data.length % frame)
					expect(Buffer.concat(out)).toEqual(data.subarray(0, whole))
					expect(remainder).toEqual(data.subarray(whole))
				},
			),
			{ numRuns: 100 },
		)
	})

	it.each([
		["S16_IQ", 4],
		["FLOAT32LE", 8],
	] as const)("drops the unmatched tail of a %s recording at each loop boundary", async (format, frame) => {
		const directory = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "wavekit-iq-"))
		const path = join(directory, `odd-${format}.bin`)
		const whole = Buffer.from(Array.from({ length: 2 * frame }, (_, n) => n + 1))
		writeFileSync(path, Buffer.concat([whole, Buffer.from([0xee, 0xee, 0xee])]))
		const manager = new SourceManager(pino({ level: "silent" }))
		try {
			const stream = await manager.connect({
				id: `loop-${format}`,
				type: "recording",
				filePath: path,
				loop: true,
				playbackSpeed: 1,
				caps: { kind: "iq", format, sampleRate: 2048000, exclusive: false },

			const chunks: Buffer[] = []

			expect(chunks.every(chunk => chunk.equals(whole))).toBe(true)
		} finally {
			await manager.disconnectAll()
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Above `export class SourceManager` in `src/core/source-manager.ts`, add:

```ts
/**
 * Bytes per complex sample for IQ formats (CU8 pair 2, CS16 pair 4, CF32
 * pair 8); null for audio and undeclared formats, which are not aligned.
 */
export function iqFrameBytes(
	caps: Pick<SourceCaps, "kind" | "format">,
): number | null {
	if (caps.kind !== "iq") return null
	switch (caps.format) {
		case "U8_IQ":
			return 2
		case "S16_IQ":
			return 4
		case "FLOAT32LE":
			return 8
		default:
			return null
	}
}

/** Prepends the carried remainder and cuts `chunk` to whole frames. */
export function alignIqChunk(
	remainder: Buffer,
	chunk: Buffer,
	frameBytes: number,
): { aligned: Buffer; remainder: Buffer } {
	const input = remainder.length ? Buffer.concat([remainder, chunk]) : chunk
	const length = input.length - (input.length % frameBytes)
	return {
		aligned: input.subarray(0, length),
		remainder: Buffer.from(input.subarray(length)),
	}
}
```

In `forwardData`, replace the block from the comment `// TCP boundaries are arbitrary.` through the closing `}` of `if (state.config.caps.kind === "iq" && state.config.caps.format === "U8_IQ") { … }` with:

```ts
		// TCP boundaries are arbitrary. Fanout may shed complete chunks, so each
		// IQ chunk must contain whole complex samples before reaching its branches.
		const frameBytes = iqFrameBytes(state.config.caps)
		if (frameBytes !== null) {
			const { aligned, remainder } = alignIqChunk(
				state.iqRemainder,
				chunk,
				frameBytes,
			)
			state.iqRemainder = remainder
			chunk = aligned
			if (!chunk.length) return true
		}
```

The three existing `state.iqRemainder = Buffer.alloc(0)` resets (loop restart, reconnect, caps reset) stay as they are. If `SourceCaps` is imported as a type from `../config.js` in this file, the helper signature uses that same alias.

```ts
	const reconnect = () => {
		transport.frames.length = 0
		return controller.synchronizeOnConnect("rtl-1")
	}

	it("never replays test mode set through the API, even left on", async () => {
		await controller.setFrequency("rtl-1", 446_000_000)
		await controller.setTestMode("rtl-1", true)
		expect(controller.getState("rtl-1")?.testMode).toBe(true) // reported, not desired
		expect(controller.getState("rtl-1")?.unknownFields ?? []).not.toContain("testMode") // known (inferred)
		reconnect()
		expect(transport.frames).toEqual([[SET_FREQUENCY, 446_000_000]])
	})

	it("never replays test mode observed from the relay", () => {
		controller.applyExternalCommand("rtl-1", SET_TEST_MODE, 1)
		expect(controller.getState("rtl-1")?.testMode).toBe(true)
		expect(controller.getState("rtl-1")?.unknownFields ?? []).not.toContain("testMode")
		reconnect()
		expect(transport.frames.some(([cmd]) => cmd === SET_TEST_MODE)).toBe(false)
	})

	it("writes a marker sequence on the wire in order and accepts only the frequency", async () => {
		await controller.setTestMode("rtl-1", true, { origin: "scanner" })
		await controller.setFrequency("rtl-1", 412_600_000, { origin: "scanner" })
		await controller.setTestMode("rtl-1", false, { origin: "scanner" })
		expect(transport.frames).toEqual([
			[SET_TEST_MODE, 1],
			[SET_FREQUENCY, 412_600_000],
			[SET_TEST_MODE, 0],
		])
		reconnect()
		expect(transport.frames).toEqual([[SET_FREQUENCY, 412_600_000]])
	})

	it("accept: false writes and updates state and caps, marks the field known, but is not replayed", async () => {
		await controller.setFrequency("rtl-1", 433_920_000, { origin: "scanner", accept: false })
		await controller.setGain("rtl-1", 300, { origin: "scanner", accept: false })
		expect(controller.getState("rtl-1")?.frequency).toBe(433_920_000)
		expect(transport.caps.centerFreq).toBe(433_920_000)
		expect(controller.getState("rtl-1")?.unknownFields ?? []).not.toContain("gain")
		reconnect()
		expect(transport.frames.some(([cmd]) => cmd === SET_FREQUENCY || cmd === SET_GAIN)).toBe(false)
	})

	it("accept: false after an earlier accepted write replays the current value (replay encodes state)", async () => {
		await controller.setFrequency("rtl-1", 145_000_000)
		await controller.setFrequency("rtl-1", 433_920_000, { origin: "scanner", accept: false })
		reconnect()
		expect(transport.frames).toEqual([[SET_FREQUENCY, 433_920_000]])
	})

	it("reports the origin of every write; untagged writes report none", async () => {
		await controller.setFrequency("rtl-1", 145_000_000, { origin: "rest" })
		await controller.setGain("rtl-1", 300, { origin: "scanner" })
		await controller.setPpm("rtl-1", 1)
		expect(sent).toEqual([
			{ command: "set-frequency", value: 145_000_000, origin: "rest" },
			{ command: "set-gain", value: 300, origin: "scanner" },
			{ command: "set-freq-correction", value: 1, origin: undefined },
		])
	})

	it("configure tags each command it sends", async () => {
		await controller.configure("rtl-1", { frequency: 144_800_000, gainMode: "manual", gain: 250 }, { origin: "rest" })
		expect(sent.map(s => s.origin)).toEqual(["rest", "rest", "rest"])
	})

	it("reconnect replay reports origin replay", async () => {
		await controller.setFrequency("rtl-1", 145_500_000, { origin: "scanner" })
		sent.length = 0
		reconnect()
		expect(sent).toEqual([{ command: "set-frequency", value: 145_500_000, origin: "replay" }])
	})
})
```

```ts
	async setFrequency(

		this.validateRange("frequency", hz, VALIDATION.frequency)
		await this.sendCommand(sourceId, RTL_TCP_COMMANDS.SET_FREQUENCY, hz, opts)
		state.frequency = hz
		this.sourceManager.updateSourceCaps(sourceId, { centerFreq: hz })
		this.emitStateChanged(sourceId)
	}
```

```ts
/** The reported TunerState field a command writes, if it has one (rtlXtal, tunerXtal and tunerGainIndex do not). */
function stateFieldOf(cmd: number): TunerStateField | undefined {
	if (cmd === RTL_TCP_COMMANDS.SET_TEST_MODE) return "testMode"
	const field = COMMAND_FIELDS[cmd]
	return STATE_FIELDS.find(known => known === field)
}
```

```ts
	/**

	 * relay TEST_MODE) is known: the state shows it. It is not a desired field.
	 */
	private markWrittenNotAccepted(sourceId: string, cmd: number): void {
		const field = stateFieldOf(cmd)
		if (field !== undefined) this.markInferred(sourceId, field)
	}
```

In `applyExternalCommand`, inside `if (updated) {`, replace `this.markAccepted(sourceId, command)` with:

Replace `sendCommand` with:

```ts
	private async sendCommand(
		sourceId: string,
		cmd: number,
		value: number,
		opts: TunerWriteOptions = {},
	): Promise<void> {
		try {
			this.sourceManager.writeToSource(sourceId, this.encodeFrame(cmd, value))
			if (opts.accept === false) this.markWrittenNotAccepted(sourceId, cmd)
			else this.markAccepted(sourceId, cmd)
			const state = this.tunerStates.get(sourceId)
			if (state) {
				state.commandCount++
				state.lastCommandAt = new Date().toISOString()
				delete state.lastError
			}
			const cmdName = COMMAND_NAMES[cmd] ?? `cmd-0x${cmd.toString(16)}`
			this.emit("command-sent", sourceId, cmdName, value, opts.origin)
			this.log.debug(
				{ sourceId, command: cmdName, value, origin: opts.origin },
				"Command sent",
			)
		} catch (err) {
			const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
			const state = this.tunerStates.get(sourceId)
			if (state) {
				state.lastError = message
			}
			this.log.error({ sourceId, err: message }, "Failed to send tuner command")
			this.emit(
				"error",
				sourceId,
				err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(message),
			)
			this.emitStateChanged(sourceId)
			throw err
		}
	}
```

`desiredFields` stores only an acceptance sequence per field, and replay encodes the current `state` value. So an `accept: false` write never creates a desired field, but it does not remove one either: if the same field was accepted earlier, reconnect replay re-sends the field's current (newest written) value. Only test mode is guaranteed never to be replayed, because it is no longer a `DesiredField` at all. The scanner relies on nothing more: it sends only test mode with `accept: false`; its frequency/gain hops are ordinary accepted writes, and the lease snapshot (Task 33), not replay, restores the operator's values on release.

```ts
// tests/unit/decoders/dsd-fme-link.test.ts
/**
 * dsd-fme link-control lines for the scanner (spec § 6.4) and the CRC-ERR
 * identity/encryption fix: garbage lines on key-up (run8) must not start a
 * call, set its talkgroup, or mark a clear call encrypted.
 */
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest"
import * as fs from "node:fs"
import * as os from "node:os"
import * as path from "node:path"
import pino from "pino"
import {
	DsdFmeDecoder,
	dsdFmeUdpChannels,
} from "../../../src/decoders/builtin/dsd-fme.js"
import type { DsdFmeLinkLine } from "../../../src/decoders/builtin/dsd-fme-link.js"
import type { DecoderConfig, DecoderOutput } from "../../../src/decoders/types.js"

const logger = pino({ level: "silent" })
const T0 = Date.parse("2026-10-09T20:12:54.000Z")

type Internals = {
	handleOutputLine(line: string): void
	checkCallTimeoutAsync(): void
	buildPipelineCommand(): string
	schedulePrune(delayMs: number): void
}

function createDecoder(options: Record<string, unknown> = {}): DsdFmeDecoder {
	const config: DecoderConfig = { id: "dsd-fme", type: "dsd-fme", enabled: true, options: { mode: "auto", ...options } }
	return new DsdFmeDecoder(config, logger)
}

function replay(decoder: DsdFmeDecoder, lines: Array<{ atMs: number; text: string }>, untilMs: number) {
	const outputs: DecoderOutput[] = []
	const links: DsdFmeLinkLine[] = []
	decoder.on("output", (output: DecoderOutput) => outputs.push(output))
	decoder.on("link", (line: DsdFmeLinkLine) => links.push(line))
	const internals = decoder as unknown as Internals
	let index = 0
	for (let now = 0; now <= untilMs; now += 10) {
		while (index < lines.length && lines[index]!.atMs <= now) {
			vi.setSystemTime(T0 + lines[index]!.atMs)
			internals.handleOutputLine(lines[index]!.text)
			index++
		}
		vi.setSystemTime(T0 + now)
		if (now % 500 === 0) internals.checkCallTimeoutAsync()
	}
	return { outputs, links }
}

const starts = (outputs: DecoderOutput[]) =>
	outputs
		.filter(o => o.type === "call_start")
		.map(o => o.data as { talkgroup: number | null; source: number | null; encrypted?: boolean; flags?: { wavFileUpdate?: boolean } })
		.filter(d => !d.flags?.wavFileUpdate)
const ends = (outputs: DecoderOutput[]) =>
	outputs
		.filter(o => o.type === "call_end")
		// call_end carries encryption only under data.flags (dsd-fme.ts endCall); call_start also has a top-level copy
		.map(o => o.data as { talkgroup: number | null; flags?: { encrypted?: boolean; wavFileUpdate?: boolean } })
		.filter(d => !d.flags?.wavFileUpdate)

const SYNC = (cc: string, burst: string) => `20:12:54 Sync: +DMR MS/DM MODE/MONO | Color Code=${cc} | ${burst} `
const CLEAN = " SLOT 1 TGT=9 SRC=2060945 Group Call "

/** run8 key-up garbage, then the clean call; `headerAtMs` is when the clean header arrives. */
function keyUp(headerAtMs: number) {
	const lines = [
		{ atMs: 0, text: SYNC("XX", "MBCC (FEC ERR)") },
		{ atMs: 30, text: SYNC("05", "VLC") },
		{ atMs: 60, text: "SLOT 1 TGT=11 SRC=10101393 Group Encrypted Call   (CRC ERR) " },
		{ atMs: headerAtMs, text: SYNC("01", "VLC") },
		{ atMs: headerAtMs, text: CLEAN },
	]
	for (let t = headerAtMs + 360; t < headerAtMs + 3000; t += 360) {
		lines.push({ atMs: t, text: SYNC("01", "VC*") }, { atMs: t, text: CLEAN })
	}
	lines.push({ atMs: headerAtMs + 3100, text: SYNC("01", "TLC") }, { atMs: headerAtMs + 3100, text: CLEAN })
	return lines
}

describe("CRC-ERR lines never set call identity or encryption", () => {
	beforeEach(() => {
		vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["Date"] })
		vi.setSystemTime(T0)
	})
	afterEach(() => {
		vi.useRealTimers()
	})

	it.each([130, 400])("run8 key-up garbage with the clean header at %i ms yields one clear call TG 9", headerAtMs => {
		const { outputs } = replay(createDecoder(), keyUp(headerAtMs), headerAtMs + 4000)
		const s = starts(outputs)
		expect(s).toHaveLength(1)
		expect(s[0]).toMatchObject({ talkgroup: 9, source: 2060945 })
		expect(s[0]?.encrypted ?? false).toBe(false)
		expect(ends(outputs).every(e => e.flags?.encrypted !== true)).toBe(true)
	})

	it("a corrupted encrypted line inside a clear call neither marks it encrypted nor splits it", () => {
		const lines = keyUp(130)
		lines.push(
			{ atMs: 1500, text: "SLOT 1 TGT=9 SRC=2060945 Group Encrypted Call   (CRC ERR) " },
			{ atMs: 1600, text: "SLOT 1 TGT=4711 SRC=99 Group Encrypted Call   (CRC ERR) " },
		)
		lines.sort((a, b) => a.atMs - b.atMs)
		const { outputs } = replay(createDecoder(), lines, 5000)
		expect(starts(outputs)).toHaveLength(1)
		const e = ends(outputs)
		expect(e).toHaveLength(1)
		expect(e[0]?.flags?.encrypted ?? false).toBe(false)
	})

	it("a clean encrypted line still marks the call encrypted", () => {
		const lines = keyUp(130)
		lines.push({ atMs: 1500, text: " SLOT 1 TGT=9 SRC=2060945 Group Encrypted Call " })
		lines.sort((a, b) => a.atMs - b.atMs)
		const { outputs } = replay(createDecoder(), lines, 5000)
		expect(ends(outputs)[0]?.flags?.encrypted).toBe(true)
	})
})

describe("link events (spec § 6.4)", () => {
	beforeEach(() => {
		vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["Date"] })
		vi.setSystemTime(T0)
	})
	afterEach(() => {
		vi.useRealTimers()
	})

	it("emits one link per DMR link-control line, CRC-ERR lines flagged, unparsable CC skipped", () => {
		const { links } = replay(createDecoder(), keyUp(130).slice(0, 5), 200)
		expect(links.map(({ at: _at, ...rest }) => rest)).toEqual([
			{ protocol: "dmr", cc: 5, crcErr: false },
			{ protocol: "dmr", tg: "11", src: "10101393", slot: 1, crcErr: true, encrypted: true },
			{ protocol: "dmr", cc: 1, crcErr: false },
			{ protocol: "dmr", tg: "9", src: "2060945", slot: 1, crcErr: false },
		])
		expect(links.every(l => l.at >= T0 && l.at <= T0 + 200)).toBe(true)
	})

	it("normalises zero-padded DMR voice event ids", () => {
		const { links } = replay(createDecoder(), [
			{ atMs: 0, text: SYNC("01", "VLC") },
			{ atMs: 10, text: "DMR Voice TGT: 00009001; SRC: 00001133; slot2" },
		], 50)
		expect(links[1]).toMatchObject({ protocol: "dmr", tg: "9001", src: "1133", slot: 2, crcErr: false })
	})

	it("emits P25 NAC/TG/SRC, NXDN RAN and D-STAR callsign lines", () => {
		const { links } = replay(createDecoder(), [
			{ atMs: 0, text: "Sync: +P25p1 " },
			{ atMs: 10, text: " nac: [ 1B] src: [   1234] tg: [  56] " },
			{ atMs: 20, text: "Sync: +NXDN96 " },
			{ atMs: 30, text: " VOICE RAN=50 TGT=7 SRC=8 " },
			{ atMs: 40, text: "Sync: +DSTAR " },
			{ atMs: 50, text: " MY: DL1ABC UR: CQCQCQ RPT1: DB0XYZ B " },
		], 100)
		expect(links.map(({ at: _at, ...rest }) => rest)).toEqual([
			{ protocol: "p25", nac: "1B", tg: "56", src: "1234", crcErr: false },
			{ protocol: "nxdn", ran: 50, tg: "7", src: "8", crcErr: false },
			{ protocol: "dstar", callsign: "DL1ABC", crcErr: false },
		])
	})
})

describe("modes and recording retention", () => {
	it("nxdn48 runs -fi, dpmr runs -fm, nxdn stays -fn; all are mono voice", () => {
		const args = (mode: string) => (createDecoder({ mode }) as unknown as Internals).buildPipelineCommand()
		expect(args("nxdn48")).toMatch(/(^|\s)-fi(\s|$)/)
		expect(args("dpmr")).toMatch(/(^|\s)-fm(\s|$)/)
		expect(args("nxdn")).toMatch(/(^|\s)-fn(\s|$)/)
		expect(dsdFmeUdpChannels("nxdn48")).toBe(1)
		expect(dsdFmeUdpChannels("dpmr")).toBe(1)
	})

	describe("perCallRecordingPrune", () => {
		let dir: string
		const expired = "20261009_133838_10001_DMR_CC_1_GROUP_TGT_9_SRC_1.wav"
		beforeEach(() => {
			dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "wavekit-dsd-prune-"))
			const file = path.join(dir, expired)
			fs.writeFileSync(file, Buffer.alloc(1024))
			const old = (Date.now() - 10 * 3_600_000) / 1000
			fs.utimesSync(file, old, old)
		})
		afterEach(() => {
			fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })
		})
		const options = (extra: Record<string, unknown>) => ({
			enablePerCallRecording: true,
			perCallRecordingDir: dir,
			perCallRecordingMaxAgeHours: 1,
			...extra,
		})

		it("prunes by default", async () => {
			;(createDecoder(options({})) as unknown as Internals).schedulePrune(0)
			await vi.waitFor(() => expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, expired))).toBe(false))
		})

		it("keeps every file when disabled (scanner probe recordings)", async () => {
			;(createDecoder(options({ perCallRecordingPrune: false })) as unknown as Internals).schedulePrune(0)
			await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 100))
			expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, expired))).toBe(true)
		})
	})
})
```

Replace `handleProtocolLine` with:

```ts
	private handleProtocolLine(line: string, now: Date): DecoderOutput | null {
		// A CRC-error line keeps the ongoing call alive but never sets identity,
		// starts or switches a call, or marks one encrypted (run8 key-up garbage).
		if (CRC_ERR.test(line)) {
			this.touchOngoing(now)
			return null
		}
		switch (this.currentProtocol) {
			case "dmr":
				return this.handleDmrLine(line, now)
			case "p25p1":
				return this.handleP25P1Line(line, now)
			case "p25p2":
				return this.handleP25P2Line(line, now)
			case "nxdn48":
			case "nxdn96":
				return this.handleNxdnLine(line, now)
			case "ysf":
				return this.handleYsfLine(line, now)
			case "dstar":
				return this.handleDStarLine(line, now)
			case "provoice":
				return this.handleProVoiceLine(line, now)
			default:
				// No protocol detected yet, try to extract metadata anyway
				return this.handleUnknownProtocol(line, now)
		}
	}

	/** Keeps the ongoing call of the current protocol from timing out. */
	private touchOngoing(now: Date): void {
		const ongoing = this.callState ?? this.pendingCall?.state ?? null
		if (ongoing && ongoing.protocol === this.currentProtocol) {
			ongoing.lastUpdate = now
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Parses one link-control line of the line's own sync protocol (or the
	 * current one). Returns null for lines without identity fields.
	 */
	private parseLinkLine(line: string, at: number): DsdFmeLinkLine | null {
		const sync = SYNC_PATTERN.exec(line)
		const protocol = sync?.groups
			? this.parseProtocol(sync.groups["proto"] ?? "")
			: this.currentProtocol
		const crcErr = CRC_ERR.test(line)
		const fecErrs = line.match(FEC_ERR_ALL)?.length ?? 0
		const base = { crcErr, at, ...(fecErrs > 0 ? { fecErrs } : {}) }
		const ids = (groups: Record<string, string> | undefined, tg: string, src: string) =>
			groups
				? {
						tg: String(parseInt(groups[tg] ?? "0", 10)),
						src: String(parseInt(groups[src] ?? "0", 10)),
					}
				: {}
		switch (protocol) {
			case "dmr": {
				const cc = DMR_COLOR_CODE.exec(line)?.groups?.["cc"]
				const idGroups =
					DMR_VOICE_EVENT.exec(line)?.groups ?? DMR_TGT_SRC.exec(line)?.groups
				if (cc === undefined && idGroups === undefined) return null
				const slotText =
					DMR_SLOT_INLINE.exec(line)?.groups?.["slot"] ??
					DMR_SLOT_WORD.exec(line)?.groups?.["slot"]
				const svc = DMR_TLC_FIELDS.exec(line)?.groups?.["svc"]
				const alg = ALG_ID.exec(line)?.groups?.["alg"]
				const encrypted =
					(idGroups !== undefined && DMR_ENCRYPTED.test(line)) ||
					(svc !== undefined && (parseInt(svc, 16) & DMR_SVC_PRIVACY) !== 0) ||
					(alg !== undefined && !isClearAlgorithm(alg))
				return {
					protocol: "dmr",
					...(cc !== undefined ? { cc: parseInt(cc, 10) } : {}),
					...ids(idGroups, "tgt", "src"),
					...(slotText === "1" ? { slot: 1 as const } : slotText === "2" ? { slot: 2 as const } : {}),
					...base,
					...(encrypted ? { encrypted: true } : {}),
				}
			}
			case "p25p1":
			case "p25p2": {
				const nac = P25_NAC.exec(line)?.groups?.["nac"]
				const idGroups = P25_SRC_TG.exec(line)?.groups ?? P25P2_VCH.exec(line)?.groups
				const alg = ALG_ID.exec(line)?.groups?.["alg"]
				if (nac === undefined && idGroups === undefined && alg === undefined) return null
				return {
					protocol: "p25",
					...(nac !== undefined ? { nac: nac.toUpperCase() } : {}),
					...ids(idGroups, "tg", "src"),
					...base,
					...(alg !== undefined && !isClearAlgorithm(alg) ? { encrypted: true } : {}),
				}
			}
			case "nxdn48":
			case "nxdn96": {
				const ran = NXDN_RAN.exec(line)?.groups?.["ran"]
				const idGroups = NXDN_TGT_SRC.exec(line)?.groups
				if (ran === undefined && idGroups === undefined) return null
				return {
					protocol: "nxdn",
					...(ran !== undefined ? { ran: parseInt(ran, 10) } : {}),
					...ids(idGroups, "tgt", "src"),
					...base,
				}
			}
			case "ysf":
				return /\bFICH\b/i.test(line) ? { protocol: "ysf", ...base } : null
			case "dstar": {
				const my = DSTAR_MY.exec(line)?.groups?.["val"]?.trim()
				return my ? { protocol: "dstar", callsign: my, ...base } : null
			}
			default:
				return null
		}
	}
```

The test compares link objects with `toEqual`, so key order is irrelevant; the run8 `Color Code=05 | VLC` line is reported as a clean CC 5 (it has no CRC flag), which is why the interpreter (Task 18) needs two matching clean lines. `DSTAR_MY` captures up to 8 characters, so `"DL1ABC UR"` cannot be captured: the regex value class includes a space, so if the test's D-STAR expectation fails with `"DL1ABC U"`, keep the existing regex (it is shared with call metadata) and trim to the first space in `parseLinkLine`: `callsign: my.split(" ")[0]`.

### Task 29: DecoderManager — ephemeral probes, created/removed events, source hold, route guards

**Spec:** § 6.5 (probes), § 10.4 (decoder hold), § 12.4. **Depends on:** 25, 23 (delta: `CoreSuspensionReason`, E10b). **Batch:** S1-B

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/decoders/manager.ts` (imports; `DecoderState`; `DecoderStartIntent`; `DecoderManagerEvents`; `heldSources` field; `capsWorkerRunning` → `capsWork` chain in `drainCapsChanges`; `createDecoder` → `registerDecoder`; new `createEphemeralDecoder`, `removeEphemeralDecoder`, `holdSource`, `releaseSource`, `isSourceHeld`, private `evaluateSourceNow`, `heldReason`, `assertNotHeld`; `startDecoder`; `restartDecoder`; `getStatus`; `removeDecoder`; `handleDecoderExit`; `wireDecoderToFanout`; `unwireDecoderFromFanout`; `handleCapsChange`; `assessEligibility`)
- Modify: `src/api/routes/decoders.ts` (new exported `scannerOwnedConflict`; start/stop/restart handlers, which pass `refuseIfHeld: true`; restart response schema), `src/api/routes/decoder-band.ts` (PUT/DELETE handlers)
- Test: `tests/unit/decoders/manager-scanner.test.ts`, `tests/unit/api/decoder-scanner-guards.test.ts`

Design points (consumed by Tasks 33–35):
- `createEphemeralDecoder` creates **and starts** the probe and resolves after `decoder.start()`; on failure (including a `wireDecoderToFanout` outcome with `wired: false`) it removes the instance and rethrows. With `input`, the decoder reads that Readable instead of a fanout branch; the source is still assigned, so `status.sourceId` is set and caps (`inputSampleRate`, `inputCenterFreq`) are applied. The input is attached only **after** `decoder.start()` resolved: `BaseDecoder.attachInput` adds a `data` listener (the stream starts flowing on the next tick) and pipes to stdin only when a process exists, so attaching before the spawn would drain the pre-roll the probe pool already wrote into the byte counter (spec § 6.5).
- Probes are skipped by caps evaluation (no suspension, resume or adapt-restart: the probe pool stops them on every epoch, H5), are never auto-restarted after an exit (health `faulted`, `desiredRunning: false`, `decoder:status-changed`), and ignore holds, band checks and pins.
- `createDecoder`/`removeDecoder` emit `decoder:created`/`decoder:removed` for every decoder (boot creation happens before any WS client exists).
- Holds are keyed by holder (the scanner job id): `heldSources: Map<sourceId, Set<holderId>>`, so releasing one job's hold never ends another job's (a preempted job releases on cancel/dispose). The hold check is the first rule of `assessEligibility`, so the start path, the suspended branch of `evaluateRate` (including the channelizer's E10b guard, which reads `blockedBy`) and the resume path all see it.
- `holdSource`/`releaseSource` return a Promise and apply **immediately**, not through the 300 ms `enqueueSourceEvaluation` debounce: every scanner hop emits `caps-changed`, which re-arms that single debounce timer, so with hops faster than 300 ms the debounced drain would never run during a sweep. They queue the source's current caps and drain the serial caps worker at once (`drainCapsChanges` becomes a promise chain, so the call resolves after that source's decoders were suspended or resumed). The runner awaits `holdSource` before its first retune.
- `startDecoder(id, { startMode, refuseIfHeld: true })` and `restartDecoder(id, { refuseIfHeld: true })` throw `SOURCE_HELD_BY_SCANNER` (the REST routes' 409, spec § 10.4). Without the flag (`startAll`, internal restarts) a start on a held source takes the existing suspended-start path: the intent is recorded, the decoder is suspended with `tuner-scanning` and resumes on release.

```ts
// tests/unit/decoders/manager-scanner.test.ts
/**
 * Signal discovery spec § 6.5 and § 10.4: scanner probes are runtime-only
 * decoders with their own input, and a sweep holds configured decoders on
 * its source once instead of suspending and resuming them on every hop.
 */
import { PassThrough, type Readable } from "node:stream"
import pino from "pino"
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest"
import { DecoderManager } from "../../../src/decoders/manager.js"
import { DecoderRegistry } from "../../../src/decoders/registry.js"
import { FanoutManager } from "../../../src/core/fanout-manager.js"
import type { SourceManager } from "../../../src/core/source-manager.js"
import type { DecoderCaps } from "../../../src/decoders/types.js"
import { WaveKitError } from "../../../src/utils/errors.js"
import { FakeSources, RateDecoder, iqCaps } from "../../mocks/rate-fakes.js"

const logger = pino({ level: "silent" })
const DEBOUNCE = 350
const iqDecoderCaps: DecoderCaps = { input: "iq", output: "text", integrationPattern: "pure_consumer" }
let sources: FakeSources
let manager: DecoderManager
let decoders: Map<string, RateDecoder>
let created: string[]
let removed: string[]
let restarting: string[]

/**
 * Mirrors BaseDecoder's input handling (base-decoder.ts attachInput/start):
 * attachInput adds a `data` listener, so the stream starts flowing on the
 * next tick, and pipes to stdin only once a process exists; the process is
 * spawned after an await inside start().
 */
class StdinDecoder extends RateDecoder {
	readonly stdinBytes: Buffer[] = []
	trackedBytes = 0
	private stdin: PassThrough | null = null
	private readonly track = (chunk: Buffer): void => {
		this.trackedBytes += chunk.length
	}
	override async start(): Promise<void> {
		await new Promise<void>(resolve => process.nextTick(resolve)) // spawn
		await super.start()
		this.stdin = new PassThrough()
		this.stdin.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => this.stdinBytes.push(chunk))
		this.input?.pipe(this.stdin)
	}
	override attachInput(input: Readable): void {
		super.attachInput(input)
		input.on("data", this.track)
		if (this.stdin) input.pipe(this.stdin)
	}
	override detachInput(): void {
		if (this.input && this.stdin) this.input.unpipe(this.stdin)
		this.input?.off("data", this.track)
		super.detachInput()
	}
}

const settle = () => vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(DEBOUNCE)
const ticks = async (n = 10) => {
	for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) await new Promise<void>(resolve => process.nextTick(resolve))
}
function createConfigured(id = "dmr") {
	manager.createDecoder({ id, type: "rate-test", enabled: true, sourceId: "rtl", options: { input: "iq" } })
	return decoders.get(id)!
}
function probeConfig(id = "scan-j1-dmr-1") {
	return { id, type: "rate-test", enabled: true, sourceId: "rtl", options: { input: "iq" } }
}

	sources.caps.set("rtl", { ...iqCaps(2_400_000), centerFreq: 446_000_000 })

describe("ephemeral scanner probes", () => {
	it("starts on the scanner's input, reports owner/job/ephemeral, and emits created", async () => {
```
